title: Heterogeneous fanout and budgeted geo-routing for reranker resilience
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Problem: Under high QPS and cross-region load we see tail latency and intermittent availability in the reranking endpoint. Single-model rerankers either meet quality targets but starve SLOs, or meet latency targets but regress relevance. Goal: build a routing and execution strategy that preserves high-quality ranking while reducing 99th percentile latency and improving availability under degraded conditions.

Proposed approach: implement a heterogeneous fanout execution pattern combined with a budgeted geo-routing policy and an upstream local-sufficiency filter. For each incoming rerank request we: 1) run a lightweight pre-filter (embedding cosine top-K) in the local region to prune candidates, 2) fan-out in parallel to up to three reranker variants (fast quantized small model, medium-performance distilled model, and high-quality full model) with per-variant circuit breakers and adaptive timeouts, 3) use a confidence-weighted merge: if a fast variant returns a ranking with confidence above a threshold we accept immediately, otherwise we wait for slower variants up to a global deadline and merge results via weighted ballot to produce the final order. A geo-routing controller selects which regions/replicas to call based on latency SLO budget, cost weight, and regional capacity signals. The budget is expressed as a per-request latency-credit and cost-credit; the router picks replicas to fit the budget and degrade gracefully if needed.

Why this is different: existing strategies rely on single-model fallbacks or simple region affinity. This design treats model heterogeneity and regional capacity as first-class routing inputs and introduces a local-sufficiency heuristic to avoid unnecessary cross-region calls, reducing cross-tenant blast radius and egress costs.

Trade-offs and risks: slightly higher aggregate CPU usage due to parallelism, increased orchestration complexity, more moving parts to observe. We'll mitigate via strict circuit breaker limits, sampling-based shadowing to validate quality, and phased rollout with feature flags per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: 99th-percentile latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% under 75th-percentile traffic compared to baseline
End-to-end relevance measured by MRR on the commercial testset degrades by <=0.5% compared to the current gold model (or improves)
Regional routing respects per-request latency and cost budget 95% of the time in synthetic stress tests
Circuit breaker prevents cascading failures: when the high-quality variant is taken out, system keeps serving at reduced quality with no more than 10% increase in errors
Rollout feature flag and per-tenant toggles available in console; telemetry surfaces model variant usage, fanout counts, and merged-confidence metrics
engineering_notes: 2026-02-03: Spike completed. Implemented local-sufficiency pre-filter prototype (Rust) that reduced candidate set by ~65% with 99% recall on sample queries.

2026-02-09: Benchmarks in perf lab: under 500 concurrent QPS local region, heterogeneous fanout reduced p99 from 820ms -> 410ms (median ~120ms). Cost model shows +8% token cost due to extra model calls; we will tune fanout thresholds to target <=+3% cost.

2026-02-16: Decided on per-variant circuit breaker parameters after Chaos run: fast-model cb: 500ms timeout, max-concurrency 250; medium-model cb: 900ms timeout; high-quality cb: 1200ms timeout and lower concurrency. Documented in internal RFC.
2026-02-20: QA tests show merge algorithm (confidence-weighted ballot) outperforms always-waiting-for-high-quality in A/B: MRR delta -0.2% while p99 improves 36%.
2026-02-24: PR opened for router: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-router/pull/142 (includes simulation harness and cost-budget solver).
2026-02-26: Security reviewed local-sufficiency filter for possible information leak; decided to log only aggregate metrics and not store raw embeddings. Security OK (no KMS change required).
2026-03-01: Next: integrate per-tenant toggle into console, add rollout plan with canary at 1% of tenants, expand synthetic stress tests to multi-region failover scenarios.
